environment._comment_time_limit: Seconds. Budget = commitment + swap delay + reversal + traverse to the OTHER target. At v = 0.01 an UNCONTESTED traverse is already 50 s, so the historical 60 would have censored essentially every run. The worst informative cell (delta = 0.5%) needs ~14 + 1 + 35 + 70 = 120 s; the floor cells need far more and CENSOR BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the measurement, not a failure -- the censoring rate is a reported quantity per cell. Matched to the RA arm's limit so the arms are censored on the same clock.
environment._comment_ticks_per_second: ARENA clock, dt = 1.0 s. MUST equal the agent's own ticks_per_second below, which sets the DDM's dt: under sensory_stream.mode 'shared' that equality is not advice but a FATAL precondition checked in models/percept_stream.py (white_rate is a RATE, so an unequal pair leaves the stream's dt ambiguous). Both are 1.

sensory_stream._comment: The white sensory noise lives HERE, upstream of the model, so eta_rate below is 0 accordingly and the DDM's noise scale becomes c = sqrt(2)*white_rate = 0.100. IDENTICAL to the RA arm's block -- the stream keys every draw by (trial_seed, kind, target_id, tick) only, so the realisation does not depend on how many internal sub-steps a model takes: this arm's n_sub = 16 and the RA's 500 field steps per tick both see one draw per arena tick. seed null is resolved per trial from the arena random_seed; frozen_sd = 0 because a frozen bias imposes an accuracy ceiling Phi(A/s_beta) that flattens every curve.

arena_0._comment_side: SquareArena reads 'side' (spanning [-side/2, side/2]) and IGNORES 'radius', so the old key was silently giving side = 1; side = 2 matches the campaign base and leaves headroom for wider angular separations.

environment._comment_post_bifurcation_swap: The world change is now a PHYSICAL arena event, not a model-internal quality relabel: the two targets exchange STRENGTH (and color) at FIXED positions, triggered by the first behavioral bifurcation event plus delay_ticks. delay_ticks = round(quality_swap.delay * ticks_per_second) = round(1.0 s * 1 tick/s) = 1, matching the quality_swap.delay this replaces. Why not a position swap: the DDM signs x by target_ids order, so exchanging positions leaves q0-q1 untouched and produces no drift reversal; exchanging strengths flips the drift SIGN while preserving |q0-q1| = Qbar*delta, so A_source 'ensemble' stays valid across the swap and ONE Bellman table per condition remains correct on both sides of it. NOTE the 'attributes' key is MANDATORY: arena._normalize_post_bif_swap_config defaults it to ('position',) when absent, i.e. silently to the no-op swap. The color exchange (red <-> green) is the on-screen sanity indicator that the world change fired. The strength reaches the model with no model changes: pack_objects_data ships get_strength() every tick -> GPS detection -> mf_target percept -> percept.s.

static_0._comment: R = 0.5 m at -30 deg; 60 deg separation from static_1. The BETTER target before the swap by construction; strengths are overwritten per condition with the mean-preserving pair Qbar*(1 +/- delta/2).

movable_0._comment_linear_velocity: m/s. Travel budget T_b = R/v = 0.5/0.01 = 50 s. This value is what makes the design work: the reversal boundary in delta scales as 1/sqrt(T_b) while the tick-resolution ceiling does not move at all, so dropping v from 0.05 to 0.01 opens a band that is simultaneously reversal-feasible and time-resolved. Matched to the RA arm.
movable_0._comment_angular_velocity: deg/s. Minimum turn radius is v/omega = 0.01/(120*pi/180) = 0.0048 m, comfortably inside the 0.05 m termination radius, so the agent can turn around after a reversal instead of orbiting outside it forever. Post-commitment motion only, and percepts are heading-independent under attention_mode 'none', so decisions are untouched.
movable_0._comment_timing: One integration step per control tick, across ticks, in per-second units (with n_sub sub-steps). BY DESIGN — see EMBODIED_DDM_PLAN.md Section 0.3. Do not add internal relaxation steps.

embodied_pure_ddm._comment_eta_rate: REQUIRED to be 0 under sensory_stream.mode 'shared': the noise is drawn upstream, and the stream's white_rate is handed back to the DDM as the noise SCALE c on both channels.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_n_sub: Integration step c*sqrt(dt/n_sub) = 0.100*sqrt(1/16) = 0.025 at the locked c and dt. Sub-stepping does NOT re-draw sensory noise: the shared stream is sampled once per arena tick and held across all 16 sub-steps, which is what keeps this arm's realisation identical to the RA's 500 field steps per tick.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_cost_ratio: c_e, the error-vs-time criterion [READ FROM CODE: _bellman_threshold sets c_e = float(self.cost_ratio)]. HELD FIXED across the whole flexibility campaign -- the swept factor here is the quality difference delta, not the criterion. It still enters the table cache key, so it must not drift between the precompute pass and the array.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_z_min: DELIBERATELY far below the historical 0.05: Section 1.3 requires the chance-level end of the curve to be measured (flagged, with the realised crossing log-odds recorded), and a 0.05 floor would replace the policy's z ~ 0.003 at c_e <= 0.1 with the floor itself. 1e-4 keeps the numerical guard without masking any grid point.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_bifurcation: Made EXPLICIT (rather than relying on the code default) because under predecision_motion 'midpoint' the heading sits on the fixed angular bisector until commitment, so the behavioral detector can only align with a target AFTER the commit heading step -- which is exactly the trigger this scenario wants. The code default is alignment_consecutive_ticks: 5, which at ticks_per_second: 1 would add 5 s of slack before the swap; 1 keeps the total offset at commit + ~1 tick of alignment + delay_ticks, close to the old quality_swap delay of exactly 1.0 s after commit.

bellman._comment_T_max: null = r0/v from the onset geometry, per condition.
bellman._comment_T_max_check_factor: Off for the bulk campaign; the precompute pass (campaign/precompute_tables.py) runs the 1.5x horizon check once per condition instead of once per replicate.
bellman._comment_N_t: Overridden per condition to ceil(T_max / 1e-3): dt = 1 ms everywhere on the grid (the boundary converges as O(sqrt(dt))). The historical 8660 was derived from the OLD velocity (T_max = r0/v = 0.4330127/0.05 = 8.66 s). Note T_max itself is auto-derived from r0/v when null [READ FROM CODE: embodied_pure_ddm_model.py, T_max = float(cfg['T_max']) if set else r0/v], so a stale N_t does NOT solve on a short horizon -- it COARSENS the grid: 43.30 s over 8660 steps is dt = 5 ms, five times the intended resolution. 43302 = ceil((0.4330127/0.01) / 1e-3) restores dt = 1 ms at v = 0.01.
bellman._comment_terminal: forced_choice | halt_sprt (BELLMAN_KNOWN_A_TERMINAL_HALT_DESIGN). forced_choice: commit at arrival whatever you believe, z(T_max) = 0 -- the terminal collapse; undecided mass becomes near-chance guesses and decision times clip at T_max, which caps the frontier's accuracy asymptote at large c_e. halt_sprt: at arrival the agent halts at the midpoint (v = 0) and keeps integrating at delay rate halt_cost_rate against the flat threshold z_halt (= myopic z* at c_tau = c_h), so z(T_max) = z_halt, accuracy tends to 1 - ER(z_halt), and decision times extend past arrival by ~D(z_halt) on average -- RECHECK time_limit at the top of the c_e grid before a halt campaign: a run that hits the limit mid-halt is censored. Known-|A| model only. The table cache key includes the mode, so both frontiers can share one cache.
bellman._comment_halt_cost_rate: c_h: delay rate while halted. 1.0 is the physical value (halted = zero progress recovers nothing). Only read under terminal: halt_sprt; other values are sensitivity knobs, and c_h < 1 voids the halt-only-at-arrival domination lemma.
bellman._comment_table_cache_dir: Set by the generator to the campaign's shared table cache (Section 7.3). null = solve in-process, the historical behaviour.

embodied_pure_ddm._comment_flexibility: Post-commitment flexibility. The boundary is non-absorbing: committed <=> |x| >= z(t), re-evaluated every tick (Section 3.6). The agent must be able to reverse BEFORE it arrives: d/v must exceed delay + 2z/A. At the campaign values d/v = 0.5/0.01 = 50 s, against a 1 s swap delay plus a post-swap return trip T_rev = 2*zeta*(c/A)^2 that is 35 s at the delta = 0.5% reversal boundary and shrinks as 1/delta^2 above it. Unlike at v = 0.05, that inequality CROSSES INSIDE THE GRID, which is the point: _check_reversal_feasibility stops being a formality and becomes a per-cell diagnostic. It reads quality_swap['delay'], which is now 0.0 because that block is disabled below, so its logged margin is optimistic by the true arena delay (bifurcation latency + post_bifurcation_swap.delay_ticks ~ 1 s) -- negligible against 50 s, but the number it prints is not the whole delay.
embodied_pure_ddm._comment_quality_swap: DISABLED: the arena now applies the world change via environment.post_bifurcation_swap above; leaving both enabled would make the two swaps cancel to a net no-op. Two consequences of disabling this: (a) pure_ddm_t_swap / dwell_before_swap / release-latency columns stay null -- the swap is instead recorded by the arena in the run's events.json via collect_swap_events; (b) _check_reversal_feasibility reads quality_swap['delay'] and now sees 0.0, so its logged feasibility margin is optimistic by the true arena delay (bifurcation latency + post_bifurcation_swap.delay_ticks). The block is kept (not deleted) purely for documentation of the value it used to hold.

results._comment_snapshots_per_second: Equal to the tick rate, i.e. per-tick rows; the code default of 1 snapshot/s (src/dataHandling.py) would under-sample the post-commitment reversal, which is the whole object of this scenario.
